correctness.rationale: For all finite m>=3 and all strictly positive real arms, integration over same versus distinct arms gives the exact piecewise quadratic tail. Its local derivatives recover L,m. Distributional third derivatives yield the signed arm-length minus pair-sum measure. A minimum-differing-length contradiction proves injectivity even if signed atoms cancel; no numerical experiment is used for the infinite quantifier. An 808-instance exact Fraction checker and independent grid integration corroborate boundary and collision calculations.

originality.rationale: No accessible source or public research record established recovery of arbitrary positive arm-length multisets of a finite metric star from only the probability law of a single uniform-arclength pair geodesic distance. The main published metric graph analysis gives only mean distance on equilateral stars, while broader reconstruction theorems require richer matrix-valued observations. The same-object persistence record is an identified residual full-text risk, not represented as fully excluded.

Unindexed or inaccessible prior inverse-geometric results might imply the finding. The literature search is not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: This determines a natural intrinsic inverse problem: unlike full random distance matrix data, only the scalar distribution of a single independent pair suffices to identify arbitrary positive-length branching metric stars. Exact cancellation of length knots with pair sums is genuinely structural, and is resolved by a constructive ordered inversion. The metric class is continuous and unbounded in arm count, while the degree-two exception is sharp. Finite-sample stability is not asserted.
